title: Introduce lightweight presubmit composer and dependency curation pipeline
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Adds a lightweight presubmit composer to speed developer feedback loops; introduces an offline dependency curation step and an opt-in staged preflight lane. No user-facing API changes.
description:
Motivation: Our presubmit pipeline has grown heavy and developer feedback latency has increased (cold bootstrap times and full-toolchain installs for small changes). This PR splits the presubmit bootstrap into a lightweight 'composer' that performs fast discovery, targeted env preparation, and an opt-in dependency curation pass that identifies churn and flags transitive hotspots. Goal: reduce premerge turnaround, make presubmit tooling language-aware, and add a safe offline curation job that can be scheduled independently from short feedback lanes.

Summary of changes (single continuous description): Add a new reusable GitHub Action (.github/actions/presubmit-composer) and a small runtime (ci/presubmit/composer.py and pkg/ci/runner/compose.go) which composes a minimal toolchain manifest per PR based on touched files, language heuristics, and cached manifests. Introduce ci/tools/dep_curator.py which runs an offline graph sweep (dependency pinning heuristics + candidate de-dupe suggestions) and emits a curated report saved to artifacts for engineering review. Add a lightweight CI image (ci/images/ci-light/Dockerfile) with preinstalled common toolchains to reduce cold starts. Add staged preflight manifests (ci/presubmit/manifest_templates.yaml) to support quick-smoke -> longtests handoff. Add tests and telemetry (tests/presubmit/* and ci/metrics/presubmit_metrics.prom) and developer docs (docs/dev/presubmit.md). Small hygiene: unify Makefile targets and add helper scripts for local dev (scripts/ci-helpers/toolchain-snapshot.sh).

Commits (high-level): 1) initial composer action + runtime shim; 2) dep curation engine and report format; 3) add lightweight CI image and manifest templates; 4) tests and telemetry; 5) docs and Makefile; 6) follow-up fixes to linting and arg parsing.

Changed areas (what reviewers should inspect): composer heuristics and caching logic in ci/presubmit/composer.py and pkg/ci/runner/compose.go; dep curation heuristics and report generation in ci/tools/dep_curator.py; CI image changes in ci/images/ci-light/Dockerfile (surface area for security review); new action contract in .github/actions/presubmit-composer/action.yml; test harness changes in tests/presubmit/*.

Checklist: [x] Adds automated tests covering composer heuristics and curation logic. [x] CI jobs added to .github/workflows/presubmit-lite.yml with staged lanes. [x] Docs updated with migration notes. [x] No runtime API changes. [x] Security review required for new Dockerfile (tagged).

Review conversation (selected): Reviewer (Evan Bloom): "Nice isolation — big win for dev feedback. Two asks: 1) can composer keep a deterministic manifest ordering (was flaky in my local run), 2) dep curator should emit a human-readable summary at the top of the artifact for quick triage?" Author (Asha Patel): "Good catches. Added stable sort on manifest keys and added a summary header to the curation report (see commit 4f3a2). Also added a unit test for ordering." Reviewer (Priya Nair): "We need to ensure the lightweight image doesn't expand our attack surface. Please pin base image and add image-scan Snyk step." Author: "Pinned base to debian:bookworm-slim and added a container-scan job in presubmit-lite.yml; left scanning opt-out on an env var for emergency reproductions." Reviewer (Jonah Weiss): "Please avoid silent fallbacks — if a toolchain isn't available we should fail fast and link to instructions." Author: "Adjusted composer to return a clear validation error and surface instructions in the action log. Added doc snippet in docs/dev/presubmit.md." Other comments: automated lint flagged a couple of gofmt issues which were addressed in follow-up commit.
notes: Merged after reviewers approved and CI green; dropped one optional telemetry debug flag in follow-up commit.
